Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City

Inglewood, California
  March 29, 2023
  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a special meeting on
  Wednesday, March 29, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into session at the hour of 9:00 a.m.
  The Acting City Clerk/Acting Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Council Members Dotson, Morales, and Mayor Butts; and
  Absent:  Council Members Padilla, and Faulk.
  City officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Christine Padilla  Staff Assistant

  PUBLIC COMMENTS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any item on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke about Agendas being made available to the public and
  the agenda item dating back two years ago. He stated that the City was still paying bills
  for the Super Bowl and requested that the public be aware of how much money was being
  made or lost from the developments. The speaker also stated that no one knows the City's
  current financial state and addressed legal fees on the Warrants and Bills.

  Emily Dixon stated that she hoped the funds provided by the contract would be used to
  make schools safer. She discussed the exposure Kelso Elementary School receives when people
  visit the Forum and SoFi Stadium. She also addressed the safety of the children playing on the
  playground, the teachers, and the staff. Additionally, she added that Kelso Elementary was an
  attractive school, and Inglewood Unified School District could gain  students versus losing
  students. Furthermore, Ms. Dixon displayed a photo of the Mayor of Los Angeles standing with
  the unions and the Superintendent of the Los Angeles Unified  School District. She added
  that residents didn’t want other schools closed and that billion-  dollar  stadiums  should
  support the school system. Finally, she requested that the Mayor and Council Members do
  something to keep students safe and stop school closures.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 23-173 APPROVED – BUFFALO COMPUTER GRAPHICS
  (BCG); RESOLUTION NO. 23-76 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2022-2023 BUDGET. Staff report dated March 29, 2023, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members approve an agreement with Buffalo Computer
  Graphics (BCG) for the acquisition of Crisis Management Software.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 23-173 in a total amount not to
  exceed $67,371.69 (includes a 10% contingency in the amount of $6,124.70); and 2) Adopt
  Resolution No. 23-76 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2022-23
  BUDGET FUND AN AGREEMENT FOR CRISIS MANAGEMENT
  SOFTWARE
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Members Padilla, and Faulk.
 March 29, 2023

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 9:09 a.m.

  Approved this 25th day of July, 2023.

  _________________________
  Angela Allen, Acting City Clerk

  ____________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
